(Marijuananews note: The earlier report that the DA had already decided to retry the Baldwins was apparently wrong.

Although there has been no formal announcement, and none is scheduled until June 14th, the latest buzz is that the DA will not retry them. He would almost certainly lose, inasmuch as the last jury was so evenly divided, and the DA would pay a high political price.

This leaves the DA with a real dilemma on the Kubbys. They had a few more plants, but their case will be very high profile, with little prospect for a conviction.)

Hung jury Dentist pot case may be retried
May 13, 1999
The Auburn Journal
elpatricio@aol.com
http://www.auburnjournal.com/
By Dena Erwin, Journal Staff Writer

A mistrial was declared Wednesday when a Placer County jury was unable to decide whether a Rocklin dentist and his wife possessed marijuana with the intent of selling it. Now the Placer County District Attorney’s Office must decide if the case will be re-tried.

A conference date to discuss the matter was scheduled for June 14. Michael and Georgia Baldwin were devastated by the decision. She cried, kept her head down and her eyes closed throughout the short proceeding as her husband held her hand. Michael Baldwin, on the other hand, reacted angrily.

Directly after Superior Court Judge James D. Garbolino announced the non-decision, Michael Baldwin lashed out at the few members of the jury who stuck around to explain their position. His attorney and supporters quickly escorted him from the area.

"Our lives are destroyed," he said. "This is a full-on Nazi prosecution."

Two weeks ago, Garbolino dismissed charges of marijuana cultivation leveled against the Granite Bay couple, both age 35. Because both possessed a physician¹s recommendation to use marijuana for medical purposes, the judge ruled they were within the guidelines of Proposition 215, the state¹s 1996 Compassionate Use Act.

The decision came near the end of the fourth day of deliberations Wednesday, when jurors issued a notice that they were unable to convict either defendant. Later, a poll taken by Garbolino showed they were unanimous in their indecision.

"We are very stuck," said jury foreman David Brownstein. "We are hopelessly stuck." Brownstein told Garbolino the last poll taken was a 6-6 deadlock for one defendant, 5-7 for conviction for the other, but did not specify which vote was for which defendant.

On Tuesday, jurors notified Garbolino they had reached a verdict on one defendant, but requested the reading of Georgia Baldwin¹s trial testimony. That was accomplished Wednesday morning.

After the trial, Brownstein, the jury foreman, said the jury got hung up on Proposition 215’s lack of specific guidelines on the amount of plants considered appropriate for personal use.

"There are no guidelines even though the law has been passed," he said outside Auburn¹s Historic Courthouse. "Unless the law is more specific, you can’t convict when you don¹t know the intent."

Another juror, who asked to remain anonymous, felt 146 plants was just too many for personal use. "I think they were using Proposition 215 to grow in excess," he said. "They had way too many plants to be using themselves. To me, there were too many plants. It was very difficult -- it could have gone either way."

One juror who identified herself only as Nina said most jurors agreed that the Baldwins were "growing more than they could use" and they agreed that expert witnesses for both sides were "biased." They also felt Prop. 215 needed guidelines. "Every county better get on their toes and set standards," she said. "I don’t think Prop. 215 is going to go away."

A visibly pleased Deputy District Attorney Dave Tellman said his office will discuss "how things were presented and review testimony and evidence." "Then we’ll make a call whether to try it again or not," he said.

Laurence Lichter, attorney for Georgia Baldwin, said the defense was "very disappointed" in the mistrial. "The judge gave us a fair trial," he said. "It should have been clear to the jury that the Baldwins had no official guidelines on how much they could grow and possess. We won’t make any deals (with the DA) our clients are innocent. We’ll try to convince the DA that it (a re-trial) would be a waste of money."

The Baldwins were arrested Sept. 23 when detectives from the Placer County Sheriff¹s Marijuana Eradication Team served a search warrant at their rural residence. Officers found 146 marijuana plants growing indoors, in various stages of development.
